svg.title: logrotate: create compared with copytruncate
svg.desc: Left, the create method: 1, logrotate renames worker.log to worker.log.1, and the app keeps writing to the same open file under its new name; 2, it creates a new empty worker.log with mode 0640 owned by taskflow and group adm; 3, the postrotate script sends SIGHUP and the app reopens worker.log, so new lines go to the new file; 4, on the next run worker.log.1 is compressed to worker.log.2.gz, which delaycompress postpones by one cycle. No lines are lost, but the app must be able to reopen its log. Right, the copytruncate method: 1, logrotate copies worker.log to worker.log.1 while the app keeps writing; 2, lines written between the copy and the truncate are lost; 3, worker.log is truncated to zero bytes and the app keeps writing to it, which only works cleanly if the file was opened in append mode, otherwise the file becomes sparse. It works with any app but can lose lines.

g.text: create (preferred)
copytruncate
1. rename worker.log to worker.log.1
2. create a new, empty worker.log
3. postrotate: send SIGHUP
4. next run: compress worker.log.1
1. copy worker.log to worker.log.1
2. lines written during the copy
3. truncate worker.log to 0 bytes
the app still writes to it through its open fd
create 0640 taskflow adm
the app reopens worker.log; new lines go there
delaycompress waits one cycle: safe if a write was late
the app keeps writing to worker.log
and before the truncate are lost
clean only if the app opened it in append mode
no lines lost; the app must support reopening
works with any app, but:
a small window of lost lines on every rotation
a full copy of the file on disk for a moment
a sparse file if the app writes at its old offset
Prefer create plus a reopen signal; use copytruncate only for programs that cannot reopen files.
